description: Marketing, sales, and support materials have started describing membership perks differently, creating confusion about what was actually promised to different cohorts. All programs and campaigns are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 40-year-old membership program manager trying to reconcile customer-facing promise drift
user_profile.context: No single team intended to mislead members, but wording changes over time have created a real gap between materials
user_profile.communication_style: Editorial and accountability-focused, wants promises compared by cohort and source

fact_sheet.fact: The 'Gold Glow' membership tier for Aura Circle has a standard annual price of $299.
The 'Platinum Radiance' membership officially includes a 'Glow Concierge' service, defined internally as a 24-hour response time for non-urgent travel and event booking.
The entry-level 'Silver Spark' tier was introduced on February 15, 2023, with a launch price of $99 per year.
The 'Summer Sparkle '23' digital ad campaign, which ran from June 1 to August 31, 2023, promised Gold Glow members 'quarterly bonus reward points'.
The 'New Year Glow '24' email campaign, sent on January 2, 2024, described the Gold Glow benefit as 'monthly bonus reward points'.
The 'Holiday Radiance '23' campaign landing page URL was auracircle.com/holiday-radiance, and it was active from November 15 to December 31, 2023.
An email sent to prospective Platinum Radiance members on December 5, 2023, had the subject line 'Your Exclusive Pass to Everything' and promised an 'AuraAccess Pass with unlimited guest privileges'.
The official internal 'Perk Definition Guide v3.1' states the 'AuraAccess Pass' for Platinum members allows the primary member plus two guests per visit to partner lounges.
Sales Script v2.1, used by the sales team starting October 1, 2023, instructs agents to describe the Glow Concierge as an 'instant, personal assistant for all your needs'.
The previous Sales Script v1.8, retired on September 30, 2023, accurately described the Glow Concierge with its 24-hour response time SLA.
A one-pager PDF titled 'Aura_Platinum_OnePager_Oct23.pdf', created by the marketing team, claims members receive a 'complimentary annual luxury gift box valued at over $500'.
The 'annual luxury gift box' perk is officially provisioned as a choice of one item from a pre-selected catalog with an average item cost of $150.
Support ticket #AC-88172, filed on January 15, 2024, by member Eleanor Vance, references the 'unlimited guest privileges' promise from the December 5th email.
In January 2024, the customer support team logged 112 tickets with the tag 'PerkConfusion', an increase from 18 tickets with the same tag in the previous quarter.
An analysis by support lead David Schmidt found that 65% of the 'PerkConfusion' tickets in January 2024 were from members who joined during the 'New Year Glow '24' campaign.
Lena Rivera, Membership Program Manager, is leading the 'Project Promise-Align' initiative to reconcile all customer-facing perk descriptions.
The deadline for Lena Rivera's initial findings report for 'Project Promise-Align' to be delivered to leadership is February 28, 2024.
The official 'Perk Definition Guide' stored on the company's Confluence space (ID: PDG-AURA) was last updated on April 10, 2023.
On September 28, 2023, Marketing Lead Marcus Thorne approved the new copy for Sales Script v2.1 via an email with the subject 'RE: Final Approval for Q4 Sales Scripts'.
A discussion in the '#marketing-sales-sync' Slack channel on September 15, 2023, shows a decision to use 'more impactful language' for Q4 materials, leading to the changes.
JIRA ticket MKTG-431, for updating the website's membership page, was closed on October 5, 2023, without a documented check against the official Confluence guide.
Between October 1, 2023, and December 31, 2023, the sales team, led by Priya Chen, onboarded 430 new Platinum Radiance members using the v2.1 script.
Support lead David Schmidt created Zendesk macro '#perk_clarification_gold_24' on January 10, 2024, to handle the influx of questions about monthly vs. quarterly points.
A quote from ticket #AC-89012 reads, 'The sales agent explicitly told me I would have an instant concierge. A 24-hour wait is not instant and not what I paid for.'
A cohort analysis shows members who joined in Q4 2023 have a 30% higher rate of contacting support within their first 30 days compared to members who joined in Q2 2023.
The primary data sources for Lena Rivera's audit are HubSpot campaign records, Salesforce sales call logs, Confluence documentation, and Zendesk ticket data.

user_needs.description: What were the two different promises made about Gold Glow bonus points in the 'Summer Sparkle '23' and 'New Year Glow '24' campaigns?
What is the official definition of the 'Glow Concierge' service versus how Sales Script v2.1 described it?
What guest-privilege wording appears in the December 5th Platinum email, and what guest allowance is listed in the internal Perk Definition Guide v3.1?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group follow-up: After identifying one discrepancy for the Platinum tier, the user is likely to investigate other known issues for the same tier.

user_needs.description: What was the increase in 'PerkConfusion' support tickets in January 2024 compared to the previous quarter?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After identifying a specific promise discrepancy, a natural next step is to quantify the customer impact by looking at support ticket trends.

user_needs.description: What percentage of the January 'PerkConfusion' tickets were from members who joined during the 'New Year Glow '24' campaign?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group follow-up: After learning about the overall increase in confusion tickets, the user will want to attribute that increase to a specific cause or cohort.

user_needs.description: How many new Platinum Radiance members were onboarded using Sales Script v2.1 and during what period?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After discovering the misleading sales script, the user's immediate need is to understand the size of the affected cohort.

user_needs.description: Who filed ticket #AC-88172, when was it filed, and what 'AuraAccess Pass' promise did it reference?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After comparing the promise vs. reality for guest passes, seeing a direct customer complaint provides qualitative evidence of the impact.

user_needs.description: What was the customer's quote from ticket #AC-89012 about the 'instant concierge' promise?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group follow-up: After reviewing one piece of customer evidence, the user is likely to ask for other examples to build their case, especially for other known discrepancies.

user_needs.description: What decision was recorded in the '#marketing-sales-sync' Slack discussion about the language for Q4 materials?
Who from marketing approved the new Sales Script v2.1 and when was it approved?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group follow-up: After understanding the initial decision to change language, the next step is to find the specific point of approval and accountability for the script.

user_needs.description: What was the claimed value of the 'annual luxury gift box' in the October '23 one-pager versus its official provisioned cost?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After seeing the quantifiable impact of known discrepancies, the user may want to proactively uncover other potential issues to get ahead of future complaints.

user_needs.description: Was JIRA ticket MKTG-431 closed with a documented check against the official Confluence guide?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After identifying who approved a change, a logical next step in a process audit is to check for related implementation failures, like a missed check against official documentation.
